idiom_name: closure or EventEmitter wrapper over amqplib channel.publish/sendToQueue and channel.consume
implementation_notes: In Node the adapter is normally a factory function returning an object whose methods implement the application-facing API, while amqplib's promise API (connect -> createChannel -> assertQueue/publish/consume) is the channel primitive; there is no listener interface to implement, so a closure and an EventEmitter replace the adapter class. The inbound direction registers a callback with channel.consume and acks explicitly; the outbound direction is channel.sendToQueue or channel.publish, whose boolean return and 'drain' signalling are the flow-control contract the adapter must honour. Keep the application-facing functions free of amqplib types (no channel or message objects in their signatures).
pitfalls: Ignoring the boolean returned by publish/sendToQueue and never waiting for the 'drain' event grows the channel's internal buffer without bound.
An unhandled 'error' event on a connection or channel crashes the process; the adapter must attach handlers and rebuild the connection after a close.
Acking before the application callback completes makes delivery at-most-once, while never acking turns a poison message into an endless redelivery loop.
